newsitem.title: INDIA: India CII wants sharp rise in number of taxpayers.
newsitem.headline: India CII wants sharp rise in number of taxpayers.

text.p: India's premier industry association, the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), has asked the government to broadbase the tax structure by increasing the number of taxpayers.
The CII said in a pre-budget memorandum to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda that to control fiscal deficit, expenditure management and tax reform would have to go hand in hand.
The memorandum, received by Reuters on Tuesday, was submitted ahead of the federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March) scheduled to be presented by Finance Minister P.Chidambaram next month.

"The tax base in India is still very narrow. Over 14 million people are under the tax net. One of the objectives for direct taxation in India is base broadening, that is increasing the universe of taxpayers to 30 to 40 million," the CII said.
The Indian government says it is committed to reduce the fiscal deficit, which stood at 5.9 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) in 1995/96, to 3-4 percent in the medium term.
The CII said the minimum alternate tax (MAT), imposed last year to plug a loophole that companies used to avoid corporate tax, could at best be an interim measure.
"The move should be towards lowering of corporate taxes and doing away with the exemptions," it said.
CII recommended a reduction in the corporate tax to 35 percent from the current level of 40 percent.
CII also suggested a simplification of the tax structure by moving towards a two-pronged value added tax (VAT) system, one at the federal and other at the state level.
CII also said companies should be allowed to buy back their shares and issue non-voting shares.
